body:
# Every Craft - 32

**Tired of Minecraft feeling the same? Need a fresh challenge? Or maybe you're just looking for a bit of help on your playthrough?** This datapack is exactly what you need! It completely transforms the crafting experience by modifying the output of almost every recipe in the game. Whether you're seeking an extreme challenge or a significant boost, "Every Craft" has a version for you.

**This version: Each craft yields 32 items!**

---

## Key Features

- **Custom Crafting Output:** Almost all crafting recipes (excluding a few hardcoded ones like boats) now consistently yield **32** items per craft.

---

## Why Use This Datapack?

- **Spice Up Your Gameplay:** Break the monotony and inject new life into your Minecraft worlds.
- **Tailor Your Experience:** Use the "1-craft-only" for an extreme survival challenge, or switch to the "64/32/16-craft" version to significantly speed up resource gathering. It can be a **powerful helper or a demanding adversary** in your playthroughs!
- **Easy to Install:** Get started quickly and effortlessly.

---

## Installation Guide

1.  **Download the Datapack:** Grab the `.zip` file for `Every Craft - 32` from the [releases page on this Modrinth page.](https://modrinth.com/datapack/every-craft-32)
2.  **Locate Your World Folder:**
    - Open Minecraft.
    - Go to `Singleplayer`.
    - Select the world where you want to add the datapack.
    - Click `Edit`.
    - Click `Open World Folder`.
    - Open the `datapacks` folder.
3.  **Install the Datapack:**
    - Simply drag and drop the downloaded datapack `.zip` file into the `datapacks` folder.
4.  **Activate In-Game:**
    - If you're already in the world, type `/reload` in the chat.
    - If you just placed the file, just enter the world.
    - You can confirm it's working with `/datapack list`.

---

## Minecraft Version Compatibility

This datapack was developed and tested on **Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.6 - 1.21.7**. Compatibility with future or past versions may vary.

---

## Unaffected Recipes

A few recipes in Minecraft are hardcoded and can't be changed by datapacks. These generally include (but aren't limited to):

- Boats
- Ender Chests
- Items obtained from smelting or other non-crafting table processes.

---
